The test image shows a stem/root junction being held by a hand. Key features:
- Distinct reddish-brown to orange-red discoloration on the lower stem/hypocotyl
- Firm, dry-looking lesions at the soil line area
- Sunken appearance to the tissue

Top candidates: Rhizoctonia (reddish-brown dry cankers at soil line) and Phytophthora (chocolate-brown stem discoloration). Let me view one reference from each top candidate.

This Rhizoctonia reference (Soybean_Dise_36) is a very strong visual match to the test image - same reddish-brown sunken lesions on the stem near the soil line with dark soil background. Let me view one more from a different class.

The Fusarium reference shows muted dark brown coloration, not the bright reddish-orange pattern seen in the test image.

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image**: Close-up of stem/hypocotyl at soil line showing distinct reddish-brown to orange-red sunken, dry-looking lesions on the lower stem, with dark soil visible in the background
- **Rhizoctonia (Soybean_Dise_36)**: Near-identical presentation — reddish-brown sunken lesions on stem, same dark soil context, same coloration pattern
- **Phytophthora**: Not a match — typically shows chocolate-brown discoloration extending further up the stem
- **Fusarium**: Not a match — shows darker brown/muted discoloration without the characteristic reddish color

The reddish-brown, sunken, dry lesions at the soil line are the hallmark of Rhizoctonia, and the reference image match is very strong.
